data.hypothesis: Combining T2’s warp-per-target mapping with T1’s source tiling may reduce repeated global source loads: each CTA stages 256 sources once and reuses them across eight target warps. The shared-memory traffic and barriers could offset that benefit, so the full candidate must be measured.

memory_lessons.applicability: These are campaign-specific search measurements, not general performance guarantees.
memory_lessons.claim: T2 was correct at 0.00014804925230338682 seconds. A correct two-way-unrolled integration measured slower at 0.00016489150859877718 seconds. T1’s correct shared-memory kernel was slower standalone at 0.0009205335376977983 seconds, but its source-tile idea may complement T2’s warp mapping.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this tiled T2 combination against the original T2 candidate, then independently confirm the best correct program.

data.notes: This adapts T1’s four-field source tile to T2’s eight-target-warp CTA. Inactive target warps still reach both block barriers; partial source tiles are guarded, self-interactions are skipped, and the mass is copied from the target unchanged. The shared allocation is 4096 bytes, matching the four 256-float planes. This new combination has not been compiled, checked, or measured yet; no speedup is claimed.
transformations: Preserved T2’s one-target-per-warp assignment, source-lane traversal, interaction expression, warp reductions, and output integration.
Adapted T1’s shared-memory source reuse using four 256-float planes for x, y, z, and mass; eight target warps reuse each staged tile.
Added block-wide synchronization around tile use, retained guards for inactive targets and partial tiles, and configured 4096 shared-memory bytes with 256 threads and 8 items per block.
